# ferrolink

**Fast, parallel link checker for static HTML builds.**

[![Powered by Sebastian Software](https://img.shields.io/badge/Powered_by-Sebastian_Software-005164?style=flat)](https://oss.sebastian-software.com) [![CI](https://github.com/sebastian-software/ferrolink/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/sebastian-software/ferrolink/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: Apache-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![MSRV](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.96%2B-orange.svg)](Cargo.toml)

ferrolink reads the output directory of a static site build and checks that
every link, asset reference, and `#fragment` points at something the build
contains. It parses every page in parallel, resolves references the way a
browser does, and maps URLs onto files the way static hosts do. It needs no
server and no network.

It was built to gate releases and deployments of
[Ardo](https://github.com/sebastian-software/ardo) documentation sites, and
works on the output of any static site generator.

```console
$ ferrolink check docs/build/pages --exclude 'v[345]/**'
v6/guide/component-playground/index.html
  line 17    broken link     /v6/storybook

1 issue in 1 file · 318 pages · 10845 internal links checked · 482 external not checked · 24 ms
```

## What it checks

- **Links and assets**: `a`, `area`, and `link` `href`; `script`, `img`,
  `source`, `video`, `audio`, `track`, `iframe`, and `embed` `src`; `srcset`
  candidates; `video` `poster`; `object` `data`; SVG `use` and `image`;
  `meta` refresh targets; `og:image`, `og:url`, and `twitter:image`.
- **Anchors**: a fragment must name an element `id`, or an `<a name>`, on the
  target page. `#top` and text fragments (`#:~:text=`) always resolve.
- **Base path**: on a site served below `/<repo>/`, an absolute link that
  forgets the prefix is reported as `outside base`.
- **Deployment files** at the site root: version paths in Ardo's
  `versions.json`, and redirect and rewrite destinations in `_redirects`
  (Netlify, Cloudflare Pages) and `vercel.json`.

Links inside comments, scripts, styles, and other raw-text elements are
ignored, as a browser ignores them. External URLs are counted, not fetched.

## Install

```bash
cargo install --locked --git https://github.com/sebastian-software/ferrolink
```

## Usage

```bash
# A site served from the domain root
ferrolink check docs/build/client

# A GitHub Pages project site, served below /ardo/
ferrolink check docs/build/client --base /ardo/

# Absolute links to your own host (canonical, og:url) are checked too
ferrolink check dist --site-url https://example.org/docs/

# Keep checking links into an archived version, but not the links inside it
ferrolink check docs/build/pages --exclude 'v3/**'

# Machine-readable output for CI annotations
ferrolink check dist --format json
```

The exit code is `0` when every reference resolves, `1` when issues were
found, and `2` when the check could not run.

### How URLs map to files

ferrolink follows the rules GitHub Pages, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, and most
static servers share. A path ending in `/` serves its `index.html`. Otherwise
the exact file wins, then `<path>.html`, then `<path>/index.html`. Lookups are
case-sensitive, as on those hosts, even on a case-insensitive local disk.

## Performance

On the 318-page Ardo documentation build (9.2 MB of HTML, 1,087 files), a full
check takes about 26 ms on an Apple M1 Ultra. The directory walk uses
[ferralk](https://github.com/sebastian-software/ferralk); pages are scanned on
every core.

ferrolink scans with [html5gum](https://crates.io/crates/html5gum), a WHATWG
tokenizer. [docs/parsers.md](docs/parsers.md) compares it with html5ever,
lol_html, and a [Ferroni](https://github.com/sebastian-software/ferroni)
regex scanner on the same workload. Build with
`--features parser-comparison` to reproduce the comparison with `--parser`.

## Development

```bash
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --all-features --locked
cargo run --release -- check path/to/build
```
